stories.title: Why did Seahawks trade for Quenton Nelson? Are the Colts just getting started?
stories.summary: The Seahawks acquired an All-Pro guard two weeks before the deadline. What does this mean for them and the Colts?
stories.detail: With the NFL trade deadline two weeks away , the Seattle Seahawks acquired All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The 4-3 Seahawks are getting an All-Pro offensive lineman to add to a potent offense. Nelson is one of four offensive players since the 1970 merger to be selected to the Pro Bowl in each of their first eight seasons. The others are Pro Football Hall of Famers -- running back Franco Harris, running back Barry Sanders and offensive tackle Joe Thomas, according to Elias Sports Bureau. The 2-5 Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last week, which promptly thrust key players into trade speculation. Nelson was the first one to be dealt, but hours later Indianapolis sent DT DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick . We asked ESPN NFL Nation Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson and Colts reporter Stephen Holder, plus NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid, how this trade impacts the Seahawks and the Colts. Why did the Seahawks trade for Nelson? Seattle's offensive line has not been a glaring weakness this season, but it hasn't been the strength that it was proj…

stories.title: Sources: Colts trade DE DeForest Buckner to 49ers in another major move
stories.summary: The Colts have traded DeForest Buckner to the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
stories.detail: The Indianapolis Colts have traded three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. This is the second major trade the Colts made with an NFC West team on Tuesday, following the trade of eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks . This marks a return to San Francisco for Buckner. 49ers general manager John Lynch has called trading Buckner to the Colts in 2020 the most difficult decision of his 10-year tenure on the job. On Tuesday, he righted that wrong. Buckner immediately bolsters an injury-ravaged defensive line on the heels of a loss in Atlanta in which the 49ers pressured Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . on just three of his 34 dropbacks. Buckner, 32, is entering the final year of his deal with the Colts and slated to become an unrestricted free agent after the season. Had Buckner signed this offseason with another team, the highest compensatory draft pick the Colts could have received was a 2028 5th-round selection being that he is an 11-year NFL veteran. With the trade, the Colts netted a 2027 fourth-ro…

stories.title: Jerry Jones teases hiring Troy Aikman for Cowboys amid ESPN contract drama
stories.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he "could and would" hire ESPN announcer Troy Aikman to a front office role with the team.
stories.detail: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones and ESPN announcer Troy Aikman were in the same building Monday, Oct. 26, for the Dallas Cowboys' victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." The two could find themselves together a lot more, according to Jones, who is entertaining the idea of employing Aikman should the former Cowboys quarterback exit the broadcast booth after the 2026 season . Jones' final question during his interview on Dallas radio station 105.3 The FAN on Tuesday, Oct. 27, was whether Jones would hire Aikman for a serious front-office role. “Yeah. Yes, I could and would," Jones replied. "It’s that simple because I do think that much of him with his basic command and understanding and knowledge of NFL football. He's certainly is qualified to do any of the things that have been mentioned. "So let me make it real clear: Troy Aikman is just getting started in his life. ... I think the world of him. ... He's outstanding. The answer is not that we're necessarily going to do anything more direct with the team at this time, but don’t rule it out. It's very possible." stories.summary: The Sunday Splash!
stories.detail: The Sunday Splash! report regarding a potential fire sale in Indy was conditioned on the C olts’ performance in their three remaining games before the trade deadline. After only one game, they tapped the "Everything Must Go" sign in the front yard. Guard Quenton Nelson, as expected, has been traded to the Seahawks. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner has been traded back to the 49ers, as expected. So who's next? Running back Jonathan Taylor has been the focal point of speculation, with ESPN linking him to the Packers, Seahawks, Broncos, and Vikings. The Vikings got the ultimate opportunity to scout Taylor on Sunday, when he accounted for 110 of the team's 218 total offensive yards in a 16-10 Minnesota win. Taylor averaged 5.3 yards per carry and went 38 yards for the Colts' only touchdown of the day. There's an obvious incentive to maximize 2027 draft picks, especially with the Colts' first-rounder committed to the Jets as the back end of the Sauce Gardner trade. teamStories.detail: The Raiders have one of their offensive contributors back. Las Vegas announced on Tuesday that receiver Dont’e Thornton has been activated to the 53-man roster off injured reserve. Thornton has been sidelined by a hamstring injury suffered during training camp. A fourth-round pick in the 2025 draft, Thornton caught 10 passes for 135 yards in 15 games as a rookie. Las Vegas waived defensive tackle Jonah Laulu from its active roster to make room for Thornton. Laulu’s roster move was reported earlier on Tuesday. Additionally, the Raiders have released receiver Jamari Thrash from its practice squad.

stories.detail: I don't think many people recall that SG/PG Dejounte Murray once averaged 21.1 PPG, 8.3 RPG, 9.2 APG and 2.0 SPG for the 2021-22 San Antonio Spurs . Those numbers were outrageous! Yeah, we knew he would not be able to replicate those numbers the following season with PG Trae Young 's immense usage in Atlanta, but Murray was still very good there. Then he went to the New Orleans Pelicans and was doing fine -- until he tore his Achilles. He played 45 games during his first two Pelicans seasons. Did fantasy managers forget the good times, or overlook them a bit? It's early in the 2026-27 season, but Murray is back to being a modest fantasy building block, averaging 20.3 PPG, 5.0 RPG and 6.3 APG -- with 2.3 SPG and 1.3 BPG! -- for a terrible team. His usage is back and the numbers are outstanding (though the block rate cannot continue). Most fantasy managers did not see this coming. I saw Murray's name mentioned as a potential bust, because he didn't shoot all that much when he finally debuted for his 14 appearances last season, and he was turning 30, and it's tough to thrive after a torn Achilles and, well, just stop it ... Murray is thriving, despite the relative mess around him, an…

stories.title: Jazz's Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) out 6-8 weeks, sources say
stories.summary: Utah will be down two more of its bigs as Jaren Jackson Jr. has a torn MCL in his right knee and will miss at least six weeks, while Lauri Markkanen is day-to-day with a sprained wrist.
stories.detail: Utah Jazz star power forward/center Jaren Jackson Jr . has sustained a torn MCL in his right knee and will be reevaluated in six weeks, the team announced Tuesday. Sources told ESPN that Jackson is looking at a six- to eight-week timetable to return from the injury he suffered Monday night. The Jazz also announced that Lauri Markkanen is day-to-day with a sprained right wrist. He also exited Monday's home loss to the Memphis Grizzlies in the first half with the injury. Utah is hopeful that 7-foot Markkanen won't miss an extended period, but the injury is to his shooting wrist, which is particularly problematic for a volume 3-point shooter. Jackson, a two-time All-Star and 2023 Defensive Player of the Year acquired in a blockbuster deal before last season's trade deadline, was injured when Grizzles guard Ty Jerome fell into him and caused his knee to buckle. Jackson played only three games for the Jazz last season after the trade before undergoing surgery to remove a noncancerous growth in his left knee. stories.summary: More Ajay Mitchell plus a deep roster means OKC will win a lot of regular season games. But the playoffs...
stories.detail: It was a devastating 24 hours in Oklahoma City. Everyone who saw Jalen Williams go down against the Clippers knew how bad it was, as Thunder GM Sam Presti put it, "This is an injury that generally we see more in football players." On top of that came the news that Cason Wallace has a torn labrum and will need to undergo surgery. Presti and OKC won't put a timeline on things, but history suggests neither player will touch the court again this season. Now what? What should we expect from the Thunder going forward? First: Expect a lot of wins. This team was without Williams for large chunks of last regular season and still won 64 games, most in the NBA. In their one game so far without their two starters (not to mention no Chet Holmgren or Alex Caruso), the Thunder still easily handled the Suns. The other change is that while the defense will still be good, it will not be elite. Instead, this is about to become an offensive team. That wins a lot of regular-season games. But what about the playoffs? And what should we look for? More Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain The Thunder have a natural replacement for Wallace: Ajay Mitchell. teamStories.detail: Plenty of intriguing storylines have emerged just one week into the 2026-27 NBA season . The defending Eastern and Western Conference champions have been shaky to begin their title defenses. The reigning NBA champion New York Knicks started the season 0-3 amid ring night drama , while the San Antonio Spurs dropped games against the Houston Rockets and Oklahoma City Thunder before recording their first win against the Dallas Mavericks , who were without Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg , on Saturday. Their struggles have allowed other contenders to take center stage, such as Luka Doncic putting up 52 points against the Utah Jazz on Sunday en route to a 3-0 start for the Los Angeles Lakers . Injuries have already started to take their toll, too. The Detroit Pistons ' Jalen Duren , the Orlando Magic 's Jalen Suggs and the Thunder's Jalen Williams all suffered injuries during opening week that will sideline them , with Williams being stretchered off the court .
